title: Custom Difficulty Slider Range
doc: CKF Hard Mode - custom-difficulty slider range.
One key, and it is the whole section - in 3.0 it is the "difficulty" section
of ckf.hardmode.json rather than the [Difficulty] section of the cfg. The 20 knobs that used to live here -
MonsterHitPointScalar, PowerLevelScalar, MissionEconomy and the rest - were
removed in 2.11.0. They were a second
place to set values the game already exposes on its own custom-difficulty
sliders, under its own names, and they had already produced a bug: two of
them shipped non-NaN, so a fresh install silently doubled enemy HP.
This section's whole job is now to widen the game's own Min/Max bounds so
those sliders reach further. Set difficulty in the game's window.
GameDifficultyModel's bound properties are STATIC, which took two failed
runs to establish: Run28 dumped a materialized row and found 66 instance
properties with not one bound among them. So widening is a one-shot on the
type at load, not per row.
[PowerLevel] is unaffected by this section. It reads the model properties
the sliders write, so it picks up whatever was set in-game.
uiDoc: This does not set difficulty. It widens how far the game's own custom difficulty sliders can be pushed. You then set the difficulty itself in the game's own window.
A ceiling is multiplied outward. A floor above zero is pulled closer to zero. A floor already below zero is pushed further down. A limit of exactly zero is left where it is.

fields.label: Slider range multiplier
fields.doc: How far past stock the game's own custom-difficulty sliders may be pushed. GameDifficultyModel pairs each setting with Min/Max properties and they are writable, so this stretches them: a positive ceiling is multiplied, a negative floor is multiplied (further down), a positive floor is divided (closer to zero), and a bound of exactly zero is left alone. 1 = leave the stock ranges alone. 3.0 moved this key out of the [Difficulty] section of ckf.hardmode.cfg and into the "difficulty" section of ckf.hardmode.json; the section is new in 3.0 and has no 2.x sidecar behind it, which is what targets.legacyJson: null records.
